question:
APIC EPG Resolution Immediacy is set to "Immediate".
Which statement is true about the Deployment Immediacy for VMM domains associated to EPGs?
options: If "On demand" is selected, the policy is programmed in the hardware only when the first packet is received through the data path.
If "Immediate" is selected, the policy is programmed in the hardware as soon as the leaf is booted.
The "Immediate" and "On demand" options require a port group to be created on the VDS.
If "On demand" is selected, the policy is programmed in the hardware only when the APIC detects a VM created in the EPG.
theory: For VMM-integrated EPGs, Resolution Immediacy controls when the APIC pushes a policy down to a leaf, while Deployment Immediacy controls when that already-resolved policy is actually programmed into the leaf's hardware policy TCAM. With Deployment Immediacy set to "On Demand," the leaf holds the resolved policy but doesn't consume TCAM space until the first data packet from that endpoint is actually seen on the data path; "Immediate" instead programs the hardware as soon as the policy resolves (e.g., when the VM's port group is created), not merely when the leaf boots. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI VMM Domain Integration)
